I loved living in Philly during grad school. There are many opportunities to meet and collaborate with local scientists. Plus there’s a wide range of inexpensive or free activities outside of science. (Big sports city, lots of museums, amazing food and beer, etc).

I had a proud moment today when I was able to drive from work to my gym without gps. It was immediately followed by the realization that I forgot to pack gym shorts. I did move to a new place, but I’m still the same person.

I might be a postdoc, but colorimetric titrations still entertain me, just like they did in high school. Back then I thought maybe one day I’d be a chemist. And well, here I am applying my general chemistry knowledge and loving (almost) every minute of it. #chemtwitter

Today's millennial horror story: finding out that one of my large student loans was not actually deferred six months after graduation, but instead required my attention two months ago. Anxiety triggered. But thanks to the woman at Wells Fargo for being kind and patient with me.

As always, I’m thankful for my wonderful family and friends. I’d like to thank you for your love and support that helped me with a whole lot of big things this year, like finishing my PhD, moving to a new city, starting a postdoc, and accepting who I am. #Thanksgiving

Our undergrads returned today & the office was filled with smiles, stories, & science. I enjoyed listening to these brilliant, young scientists plan the next steps in their research projects. I've only known them for a few months, but they've grown so much & I'm just so proud.

Today I am optimistic about the future of academia. (1/3) This evening I had a long discussion with an undergrad about lab environments. He reflected on how grateful he is that our lab prioritizes creating a culture that supports each other and pushes our research forward.

Today I voted for at ! (early voting is a great option!) Elizabeth Warren is the candidate fighting hard to improve our country for everyone, with clear plans for her presidency. That’s why she has my vote. #PresidentWarren #Warren2020 #NCPrimary

I finished my prepared material and thanked the students for their great participation (especially for 830am!) in my very first lecture, in which they responded by a HUGE applause that brought me to tears and provided a much needed confidence boost. (2/4)

Teaching students important topics and the applications to ongoing research reinforces why I want to pursue a career in academia. I shared my love of bioinorganic chemistry with students and had so much fun doing it! And now I get to jump back into lab! (4/4)

It is a relatively common at to have several additional faculty members attend. As a young grad student, I would likely have been terrified to know that a lot of faculty would attend my defense, but on that day I was truly honored that so many came to support me.

I moved to North Carolina a year ago yesterday to start the next chapter of my life as a postdoc. I knew I would miss having Philly as my home. I grew up a lot in my time there, and found ways to be okay with my mental health. It’s my happy and safe place. (1/2)

Durham has provided me a similar space. I finally accepted that I could stop trying to be I’m someone I’m not. So this year Pride Month feels extra special, as it’s my first as an openly bisexual person. 🏳️‍🌈 I made this cross stitch to celebrate. #PRIDE2020 (2/2)
Pennsylvanians deserve better from their representatives. Rather than educate himself, Rep. Moul used words the dismiss the painful experiences of Black people. Unacceptable.

I am very grateful for the Duke faculty and students that shared their lived experiences in the Black community about how racism impacted and continues to impact their lives at Duke and in the world. It is a privilege to listen to and learn from them.

Today's therapy session was extra heavy. If anyone has any tips for navigating through #grief rather than avoiding it (my usual MO), please share. Bonus points if your ideas focus on grieving the loss of a loved one to #dementia. #mentalhealth #support

My dad said things like “I don’t want my kids to be gay” many times in my life which is why I have yet to tell him that I’m bisexual and I will turn 30 next month. I don’t want to disappoint my father, so I pretend to be something I’m not to my family.
My dad saying he didn’t want gay kids told me he thought there was something wrong with being gay. That’s homophobic.
